_note: Trimmed skill descriptions for THIRD-PARTY skills, per SKILL-AUDIT-2026-09-18.md. Descriptions are the only always-on token cost: every installed skill's description loads into every session before any work. install.py fetches these 23 skills from their upstream repos, which carry the long originals, so a trim made by hand on one machine is lost on the next install. This file is that trim as re-appliable data. Run scripts/apply-descriptions.py after install.py; --check reports drift and changes nothing. Bodies are never touched, because they belong upstream and an edit there loses the next upstream fix. Target: 40 words or fewer, keeping every distinctive trigger phrase and cutting the prose around them.

apple-design.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, for the web. Use for gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion.

doc-coauthoring.description: Structured workflow for co-authoring documentation — docs, proposals, technical specs, decision docs. Use when the user mentions writing docs, creating proposals or drafting specs; helps transfer context, iterate, and verify the doc works for readers.

docx.description: Word documents and templates (.docx, .dotx): create, read, edit, find-and-replace, images, tracked changes, comments, tables of contents, headings, page numbers, letterheads. Use for a report, memo, letter or template asked for as a Word file. Not PDFs or spreadsheets.

hyperframes.description: Mandatory entry point: read first for any video, animation or motion-graphic request — promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow, interactive deck, Remotion port, HyperFrames composition — or inspect, preview, publish or batch-render one. HyperFrames is the default framework.

hyperframes-animation.description: All HyperFrames animation: atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, transitions, 24 named text effects, choreography audits, and the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, WAAPI, TypeGPU). Single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.

hyperframes-audio.description: Mixing audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition: fade-in/out, crossfade, track gain or volume, ducking, voiceover carve, effects (EQ, compressor, limiter, reverb, delay), automation envelopes, submix bus (`<hf-audio-group>`). Sourcing or generating audio is /media-use; clip timing is /hyperframes-core.

hyperframes-cli.description: The HyperFrames CLI loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, lambda, doctor, tts, transcribe. Also for diagnosing build or render failures. validate/inspect/layout are deprecated aliases; use check.

hyperframes-keyframes.description: HyperFrames punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics.

hyperframes-registry.description: Search, install and wire HyperFrames registry blocks and components. Use BEFORE hand-building any named visual — CRT scanlines, glitch, chromatic aberration, film grain, shimmer sweep, chart, terminal window, map, confetti — and for hyperframes add, hyperframes catalog, or hyperframes.json.

media-use.description: Every media need for HyperFrames: resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, colour grade or LUT into a frozen file; generate via TTS/music/image models; voiceover, transcription, captions, background removal; cut/reframe/transform; footage that looks dark, flat or should feel retro.

no-ai-slop.description: Edit drafts into sharper, more human writing while preserving the writer's voice, or detect AI-slop patterns without rewriting. Use when a draft should be clearer, more direct, more opinionated or less AI-sounding, or when asked whether writing reads as AI.

pdf.description: Anything with PDF files: extract text or tables, merge, split, rotate, watermark, create, fill forms, encrypt/decrypt, extract images, OCR scanned PDFs to make them searchable. Use whenever a .pdf file is mentioned or asked for.

pitch-deck.description: Populates investment-banking pitch deck templates with data from source files. Use when a PowerPoint template must be filled in from Excel/CSV source data, or data transferred into existing slide layouts. Not for creating presentations from scratch.

playwright-best-practices.description: Writing or fixing Playwright tests: flakiness, debugging failures, Page Object Model, CI/CD, API mocking, auth/OAuth, accessibility (axe-core), fixtures, tags and --grep, visual, component, security and performance testing, iframes, multi-tab, mobile, Electron, browser extensions.

ponytail.description: Forces the laziest solution that works: YAGNI, standard library before custom code, native features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Levels lite/full/ultra. Use on any coding task, or on "ponytail", "be lazy", "simplest solution", "yagni", "do less", over-engineering complaints.

ponytail-review.description: Code review focused only on over-engineering — what to delete: reinvented standard library, unneeded dependencies, speculative abstractions, dead flexibility. One line per finding. Use on "review for over-engineering", "what can we delete", "is this over-engineered", "simplify review", /ponytail-review.

prompt-engineering-patterns.description: Use when asked to optimise a prompt, improve prompt performance, design a prompt template, write better prompts, debug prompt issues, use chain-of-thought, structured prompting or few-shot prompting for production LLM applications.

simple-issue-description.description: Turn a rough bug report, feature request, support note or pull request into a short plain-language issue about the problem and desired behaviour. Use to simplify an issue, explain what a PR is for, strip implementation detail, or /simple-issue-description.

skill-creator.description: Create, modify and improve skills, and measure skill performance. Use to create a skill from scratch, edit or optimise an existing skill, run evals, benchmark with variance analysis, or optimise a skill's description for better triggering.

speech.description: Text-to-speech narration or voiceover, accessibility reads, audio prompts, or batch speech generation via the OpenAI Audio API; runs `scripts/text_to_speech.py` with built-in voices and needs OPENAI_API_KEY. Custom voice creation is out of scope.

ui-ux-pro-max.description: UI/UX design intelligence for web, mobile and desktop — designing, building, reviewing or fixing interfaces. Searchable local data: 79 styles, 192 product palettes, 74 font pairings, 119 UX guidelines, 105 icons, 17 GSAP presets, 25 chart types, 22 stacks.

watch.description: Watch a video (URL or local path) like an editor: scene-change frames, pacing metrics (cuts/min, shot length), 0-10s hook microscope, transcript from captions or Whisper. Produces report.md and can auto-ingest into an Obsidian vault ($WATCH_VAULT_DIR).

xlsx.description: Spreadsheets as input or output: read, edit, fix, create or convert .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, .tsv — formulas, formatting, charts, cleaning messy tabular data. Trigger when a spreadsheet is named. Not for Word, HTML reports, or Google Sheets APIs.
